title: Subtree of Another Tree
description: Given the roots of two binary trees `root` and `subRoot`, return `true` if some node in `root` together with **all** of its descendants forms a tree identical to `subRoot` (same shape and values). Otherwise return `false`.

examples.input: root = [3, 4, 5, 1, 2, null, null, null, null, 0], subRoot = [4, 1, 2]
examples.explanation: Node 2 has an extra child 0 in root, so the subtree at 4 does not match.

hints: You already know how to test whether two trees are identical.
Try every node of root as a possible starting point for that identical-tree test.
isSubtree(root, sub) = same(root, sub) or isSubtree(root.left, sub) or isSubtree(root.right, sub). An empty root can never contain a non-empty subRoot.
starterCode:
class Solution:
    def isSubtree(self, root: Optional[TreeNode], subRoot: Optional[TreeNode]) -> bool:

args.$py: [x for i in range(1,2000) for x in (1,None)]+[1]
[x for i in range(1,1000) for x in (1,None)]+[1]
[x for i in range(1,1500) for x in (1,None)]+[1]
[x for i in range(1,1000) for x in (1,None)]+[2]

solution.explanation: For each node of root, check whether the tree hanging from it is identical to subRoot using a helper that compares two trees node by node. subRoot is a subtree if it matches at the current node or inside the left or right subtree. In the worst case each of the m nodes of root triggers a comparison of up to n nodes, so time is O(m * n); space is the recursion depth.
